LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 6.1.1 INTENSIVE LISTENING

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.1: Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Intensive Listening
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Intensive Listening, part of Strand 6 in Grade 9 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How can we ensure we say tongue twisters correctly? 2. Why are riddles important in a community?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work with peers to collect varied tongue twisters and riddles from the community,

2. take turns to recite the tongue twisters,

3. work with peers to conduct a speed game to recite the tongue twisters within the shortest time possible,

4. work jointly with peers to discuss the riddling process,

5. collaborate with peers to solve riddles,

6. compose a spoken word piece (utterance) with relevant tongue twisters and riddles,

7. perform the spoken word piece during club activities,

8. organise the riddles and tongue twisters in a portfolio. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work with peers to collect varied tongue twisters and riddles from the community,
2. take turns to recite the tongue twisters,
3. work with peers to conduct a speed game to recite the tongue twisters within the shortest time possible,
4. work jointly with peers to discuss the riddling process,
5. collaborate with peers to solve riddles,
6. compose a spoken word piece (utterance) with relevant tongue twisters and riddles,
7. perform the spoken word piece during club activities,
8. organise the riddles and tongue twisters in a portfolio. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Intensive Listening together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner works jointly with peers to conduct a speed game to recite the tongue

twisters within the shortest time possible.

• Creativity and Imagination: is enhanced as the learner shares new ideas that inspire creativity when composing a spoken

word piece with relevant tongue twisters and riddles.

Values:
• Unity: This is promoted as the learner cooperates with peers to collect varied tongue twisters and riddles from the

community.

• Peace: This is promoted as the learner displays tolerance with peers when collaborating to solve riddles.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peer education and mentorship is promoted as the learner collaborates with others to recite tongue twisters and solve riddles.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of solving riddles and reciting tongue twisters to similar concepts in the study of short forms

in English.
